Gold's path to $6,000 and silver's return above $90 depend on renewed investor confidence – Metals Focus
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices continue to struggle as persistent inflation and rising interest rates drive investors toward higher-yielding assets; however, one precious metals analyst says the market is consolidating rather than entering a bear market, with the structural drivers that supported last year's historic rally remaining firmly intact. In an interview with Kitco News, Matthew Piggott, Director of Gold and Silver at Metals Focus, said that although investors have become increasingly cautious, institutional and central bank buying continues to support gold above $4,000 an ounce. His comments come as Metals Focus forecasts gold prices will average $5,330 an ounce in 2027, a 16% increase from this year's projected average of $4,600. The British research firm expects gold to average $5,600 in the fourth quarter of next year, with prices potentially approaching $6,000.

Gold and silver prices pressured by hot inflation, but gold ETF holdings buck trend to hit 2026 highs – Heraeus
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold and silver both came under renewed pressure following last week’s elevated CPI and PPI prints. Still, gold ETF demand has bucked the earlier trend to rise to annual highs despite the oil and rate headwinds. At the same time, India’s evolving import tax rules continue to impact precious metals demand, according to precious metals analysts at Heraeus. In their latest update, the analysts noted that gold prices held critical support levels last week amidst a challenging macro backdrop. “Gold briefly wicked below $4,100/oz following the September US CPI release, as the initially hawkish market reaction pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher and increased expectations for another Fed hike,” they noted. “That reaction has since partly reversed, with the implied probability of a 25 bp increase at the 28 October meeting falling and gold recovering the support at $4,100/oz as yields and the dollar have eased.”

items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Billionaire Elon Musk on Monday pledged one share of his company SpaceX to "every kid in America." The offer arrived a day after artificial intelligence company Anthropic announced in a social media post that it will commit 5% of its shares to a new "public benefit" fund.
